notes: Id-form scorecard (this is the capability documented as mixing id conventions in one call): project_id declared INTEGER (v1 route, digits only) — 379335744 worked as declared; passing 'PR-2005' was rejected client-side by invokeCapability itself ('project_id' must be a number), consistent with the declared type, no drift. test_case_id declared INTEGER (numeric case id, not TC-NNN) — 1971631/1971632/1972036/1975349 all worked as declared; passing 'TC-54455' was likewise rejected client-side ('test_case_id' must be a number), again consistent — unlike the assign_test_run_test_cases precedent, the declared type here is correct so the capability stays usable. test_run_id declared STRING accepting EITHER 'TR-NNN' (preferred) OR the run's bare integer id (pattern ^(TR-)?[0-9]+$) — only the TR-NNN form actually works. The bare-integer form, even using TR-9062's and TR-9061's own verified integer ids (confirmed correct via get_test_run_by_integer_id and via the fixture pool), produced a 400 'TRTC not found for given testrun_id:<unrelated number>' where the cited id (358823, then 358621) matches neither the id sent nor the target run — reproduced twice with different inputs, so it is a stable defect in this capability's bare-integer id resolution, not a fixture mistake or preprod flakiness. This is DRIFT, HIGH severity: one of the two declared id conventions for test_run_id does not work. Separately, error envelope: both 400s observed here were flat {success:false, message:'...'} with no `error` object, no `code`, no `details` — contradicting the declared 400 schema {success, error:{code, message, details}}. This is another instance of the suite-wide systemic error-envelope problem (previously nine capabilities / six shapes) — DRIFT, low-to-moderate severity (does not block reading, but callers cannot programmatically branch on error.code as documented). mappingId (query, declared REQUIRED but server-optional per guidance) was confirmed genuinely optional: omitting it and supplying either of TC-54457's two real mapping ids (2150387252, 2150387283) both returned 200 with no error, matching guidance over the stricter 'required' label — no drift, guidance is correct here. Comment-count baseline recorded per row (all zero, confirmed both via this capability directly and via list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id's independent comments_count field, which agreed in every case): TR-9062 (17575382) — TC-54455/1971631=0, TC-54456/1971632=0, TC-54457/1972036 (mapping 2150387252)=0, TC-54457/1972036 (mapping 2150387283, the duplicate row)=0, TC-54458/1975349=0. TR-9058 (__readonly__) — TC-54455/1971631=0, TC-54456/1971632=0. TR-9061 (17574995, batch-1 leftover) — TC-54457/1972036=0. TR-9063 (clone) — TC-54458/1975349=0 (checked directly), other 3 rows (TC-54457/1972036, TC-54456/1971632, TC-54455/1971631) at comments_count=0 per list_test_run_test_cases_by_integer_id only. Nothing in this pool has ever added a run-scoped comment, so zero everywhere is expected and proves nothing about item shape — this file is the 'before' baseline for the sibling create_test_run_test_case_comment probe; re-run this capability against TR-9062/TC-54455 (mapping 2150387253) or any row the create probe touches to verify item_shape against a real comment once one exists.
